title: How to assign an issue in Linear on Mac: assignee field, shortcuts and bulk assignment
metaTitle: How to Assign an Issue in Linear on Mac: Steps
description: Learn how to assign an issue in Linear on Mac with the Assignee field, the A and I shortcuts, and bulk assignment for lists and boards.
targetKeyword: how to assign an issue in linear on mac
intro: To assign an issue in Linear on Mac, open the issue and set the Assignee field in the properties sidebar, or click the assignee avatar on a board or list card. Press A to open the assignment menu, press I to assign the issue to yourself, or press ⌘K and search for Assign to.
tldr: Open the issue, then set the Assignee field in the properties sidebar.
On a board or list card, click the assignee avatar to change the owner without opening the issue.
Press A to open the assignment menu, or I to assign the issue to yourself.
Select several issues with X in list or board view, then change the assignee in the bulk action bar.
Private team issues go only to that team's members, and suspended users cannot be assigned at all.

blocks.text: Assigning an issue tells your team who owns the work. In Linear, the assignee is the one person or agent responsible for moving the issue forward. The steps below cover the Linear desktop app for Mac and the web app. The assignment steps are the same in both, so you can follow along in either one.
Before you assign: who can own an issue

Linear limits who can be assigned, and the rule depends on the team. Public team issues can go to any workspace member. Private team issues can go only to people who belong to that private team. If a name is missing from the list, the team is usually the reason.

Suspended users cannot be assigned at all. Agents follow a different rule. An agent must have access to the issue's team before you can assign it. Team membership for an agent is set when the agent integration is added, and an admin can change it later.

blocks.title: Check the team first
blocks.text: When a name is missing, look at the issue's team before anything else. The team decides who can own the issue.
Assign an issue with the mouse in the Assignee field

The mouse route is the one most people learn first. It works on a single issue, and you see the new owner in the sidebar before you move on. Start in the issue view, then try the faster card route once the steps feel familiar.

The Assignee field lives in the properties sidebar. Click the field, type part of a teammate's name, and pick the match from the list. Linear lets you assign by part of a name and lists every match, so a short search can return several people. Read the names before you confirm. If your team has two people with the same first name, check the avatar.

On a board or list card, you do not need to open the issue. Click the assignee avatar on the card and choose a name. This is quicker when you sort a long backlog, because the avatar shows who owns each card at a glance.
Assign with keyboard shortcuts on Mac
Keyboard shortcuts save the most time when you triage. Press A while you view an issue, or while your pointer hovers over one. The assignment menu opens, and you pick the teammate from it.

Press I to assign the issue to yourself. It works while you view an issue, or while the pointer hovers over a row in list view. It is the fastest way to claim work you plan to start today. Use A when the work belongs to someone else.

If you forget a letter shortcut, use the command menu. Press ⌘K, type Assign to, and choose the entry. The [command menu guide](/how-to/open-the-command-menu-in-linear) covers how to find other actions the same way.
Worked example: triaging new bugs in list view

Say a QA tester files a batch of new bugs in one team, and you lead the engineering work. You want each bug to have an owner before the team meets. Start in list view so every bug shows on one screen.

Hover over the first bug and press A. Pick the frontend engineer from the menu. Move the pointer to the next bug and repeat. For a bug you plan to fix yourself, hover over it and press I. This is quicker than opening every issue.

When several bugs belong to one person, select them with X on each row. Then right-click and update the assignee in the bulk action bar. Look at the selection before you confirm. A stray X on the wrong row adds that bug to the change.
Remove an assignee or hand work to an agent

To clear the owner, press A to open the assignment menu and choose No assignee. The issue then has no owner. If the owner is an agent, choose No agent instead. The same menu lets you hand the issue to a person.
Handoffs are common. When someone moves to another project, reassign their open issues in the same Assignee field. Leave a short note in the issue so the new owner knows where the work stands.
Assign many issues at once in bulk

Bulk assignment saves time when you reorganize a board. Switch to list or board view. Hover over an issue and press X to select it. Repeat for each issue you need. Then right-click one of the selected issues and update the assignee from the bulk action bar.

Look at the selection before you change anything. Bulk changes apply to every selected issue at once, so a mistake spreads quickly. If you chose the wrong rows, select them again and repeat the change.

blocks.text: Shortcuts to pair with assignment

items: ⌘ Shift Enter creates another issue with the same assignee, so a batch of new work stays with one owner.
⌘ Option . opens the issue in your last-used coding tool. Terminal-based coding tools need the desktop app on macOS.
W then O opens the Work on issue menu.
⌘K opens the command menu, where Assign to is one search away.

blocks.text: Learn A and I first. Add the others when assignment feels automatic. Learning every shortcut at once tends to slow people down, so add the rest one at a time.
Desktop app or web app: does the assignment change?

No, the assignment steps match across both. Linear's docs describe the same Assignee field and the same keys. The desktop app for Mac adds system notifications, unread alerts on the Dock, and tabs. It also has fewer clashes with browser shortcuts.

Browser shortcuts matter most for A and I. A browser can claim a key before Linear sees it, which makes the key seem broken. The desktop app avoids many of these clashes, so it is the better choice for heavy triage. The desktop app supports both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
The desktop app updates in the background. If a shortcut stops working after an update, quit Linear and open it again. Keep this in mind before you assume the keys are broken.
Plan limits and guest accounts that affect assignment

Your plan sets how many teams and issues you can work with. Linear's Free plan is $0 and includes unlimited members, 2 teams, and 250 issues. Basic is $10 per user per month, billed yearly, with 5 teams and unlimited issues.

Guest accounts are the catch. They are not included on Free or Basic. Business is $16 per user per month, billed yearly, with unlimited teams, and it includes guest accounts. If an outside contractor needs an issue, check the guest rules before you plan the handoff.
These prices come from Linear's pricing page as of this writing. Check the live page before you buy, because plans and regional prices can change.
Common mistakes and how to fix them

items: Pressing A while typing in a title or description. Finish typing, click outside the field, then press the key.
Assuming every teammate can own a private team issue. Only members of that private team can be assigned.
Looking for a suspended user. Suspended users cannot be assigned at all.
Assigning an agent to a team it cannot access. Check the agent's team access first.
Running a bulk change with the wrong rows selected. Look at the selection before you change the assignee.

blocks.text: Most failed assignments come down to team access or account status. If a name is missing or an agent will not take the issue, check the team before anything else.
What to do after you assign

Once the owner is set, the next step is usually a status change. Triage often runs in board view. Filter the list so you only see issues that still need an owner. The [filter guide](/how-to/filter-issues-in-linear) shows how to build that view.

If you still need to create issues, the [create an issue guide](/how-to/create-an-issue-in-linear) covers drafts and shortcuts. For selecting rows, read the [select multiple issues guide](/how-to/select-multiple-issues-in-linear).

faq.question: Can I assign an issue in Linear on Mac without opening it?
faq.answer: Yes. In list or board view, click the assignee avatar on the card and choose a name. You can also hover over a row and press A to open the assignment menu.

faq.question: What is the shortcut to assign an issue to myself in Linear?
faq.answer: Press I while viewing an issue, or while hovering over it in list view. The issue is assigned to you.

faq.question: Why can't I assign a Linear issue to someone?
faq.answer: The most common reasons are private team restrictions, a suspended account, or an agent without access to the team. Check the issue's team and the account status first.

faq.question: How do I unassign an issue in Linear?
faq.answer: Press A to open the assignment menu and choose No assignee. For an agent, choose No agent instead.

faq.question: Does the desktop app assign issues differently from the web app?
faq.answer: No. Linear's docs describe the same assignment steps for both. The desktop app adds system notifications, Dock alerts, tabs, and fewer clashes with browser shortcuts.

faq.question: Can I assign several issues at once in Linear?
faq.answer: Yes. In list or board view, hover over each issue and press X to select it. Then right-click and change the assignee in the bulk action bar.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to assign issues in Linear?
faq.answer: The Free plan is $0 and includes unlimited members, 2 teams, and 250 issues. Check Linear's pricing page for current plan rules before you decide.

steps.name: Open the issue
steps.text: Click the issue title in your list or board. The issue opens with its properties in a sidebar. The assignment steps happen in that sidebar.

steps.name: Find the Assignee field
steps.text: Look in the properties sidebar for the Assignee field. It shows the current owner, or no owner if nobody has been assigned yet.

steps.name: Open the assignee list
steps.text: Click the Assignee field. A list of people and agents opens. Public team issues show every workspace member. Private team issues show only members of that private team.
steps.tip: If the name you want is missing, the issue's team is the first thing to check.

steps.name: Search by part of a name
steps.text: Type part of the teammate's name. Linear matches part of a name and lists each match. Pick the right person from the list.

steps.name: Confirm the new owner
steps.text: Check the name and avatar in the sidebar. The same avatar shows on the issue's card in list and board views, so you can confirm it there too.

steps.name: Open the assignment menu with A
steps.text: While viewing an issue, or while hovering over one in list or board view, press A. The assignment menu opens. Pick the teammate from the menu.
steps.tip: If A does nothing in the browser, a browser shortcut may be taking the key first. The desktop app has fewer of these clashes.

steps.name: Assign yourself with I
steps.text: Press I while viewing an issue, or while hovering over it in list view. The issue goes to you without opening a menu.
steps.tip: Use this for work you plan to start today. Use A when the work belongs to someone else.

steps.name: Use the command menu
steps.text: Press ⌘K to open the command menu. Type Assign to and choose it. Then pick the teammate. This route works when you do not remember the letter shortcut.

steps.name: Remove the assignee
steps.text: Press A to open the assignment menu, then choose No assignee. For an agent, choose No agent instead.

steps.name: Select several issues
steps.text: In list or board view, hover over each issue and press X to select it. Repeat until every issue you need is selected.

steps.name: Change the assignee in bulk
steps.text: Right-click one of the selected issues. In the bulk action bar, update the assignee. The change applies to every selected issue.
steps.tip: Check the selection before you confirm, because the change reaches every selected issue.

troubleshooting.problem: The name is missing from the assignee list
troubleshooting.fix: Check the issue's team. If the issue is in a private team, only members of that team can be assigned. Confirm that the person belongs to that team.
A browser shortcut may be taking the key first. Use the desktop app, which has fewer clashes with browser shortcuts.

troubleshooting.problem: An agent will not take the issue
troubleshooting.fix: The agent needs access to the issue's team. Team membership for an agent is set when the integration is added, and an admin can change it.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot assign a person who has been suspended
troubleshooting.fix: Suspended users cannot be assigned. Check with your workspace admin about the account.

troubleshooting.problem: A bulk change hit the wrong issues
troubleshooting.fix: Look at the selection before you change anything. Select the correct rows again, then repeat the change.

troubleshooting.problem: A shortcut stopped working after the desktop app updated
troubleshooting.fix: Quit Linear completely and open it again. The desktop app installs updates in the background.
